transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Product) — Sara Malik (BlueForge VP Eng), Tom Reyes (BlueForge ML Eng), Priya Nair (BlueForge Infra), Liam O'Connor (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto gen maybe):
- Demo of Redwood Console focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdown.
- Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; security (VPC/KMS) and pilot sizing.
- Agreed next steps: pricing deck, console screenshots, sample traffic for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, um would you like me to kick off with a quick agenda?
[00:10] Sara Malik: yes, please, thanks Jamie. we've got about 50 minutes, main goal is to see the console analytics and how cost shows up per route and per model, and understand what a pilot would look like.
[00:22] Jamie Park: perfect. i'll keep it focused. quick intros — i'm jamie, i'm your AE. riley is our se, he'll do most of the console walkthrough and answer infra and perf q's.
[00:33] Riley Chen: hi all, hey — good to meet you.
[00:36] Tom Reyes: tom here, ml engineering. most interested in token accounting and whether we can map prompts to routes for cost attribution.
[00:45] Priya Nair: priya — infra. VPC options, KMS, and audit logs are top of mind.
[00:50] Liam O'Connor: liam from procurement, i'll mostly be listening for pricing and contract flow.
[01:02] Riley Chen: ok jumping in, i've shared my screen — this is the Redwood Console. top nav, left is usage, routes, models, and optimize. i'll open usage analytics first.
[01:15] Riley Chen: here you can see token volumes over time, broken down by model and route — so each API route you define (for example, /chat-support, /summary) appears as a line. we've got filters for customer-id, model-version, and time window.
[01:30] Sara Malik: can you show route level cost? we need to bill product teams internally.
[01:36] Riley Chen: sure — switching to the per-route dashboard. so per-route we show total tokens, avg tokens per request, estimated cost (based on your pricing tier and any committed discounts), and latency percentiles.
[01:50] Riley Chen: note: cost estimate here is model * token-price + embedding calls; we also show a rolling 30-day burn. we surface if caching saved tokens as a separate line.
[02:05] Tom Reyes: how accurate is that? like is it exact billing or an estimate?
[02:10] Riley Chen: good q — it's an estimate tied to the billing engine. for hosted customers it's pretty much one-to-one; for dedicated/reserved it's tied to committed throughput, so you see effective per-token cost which includes reserved capacity amortization. there's a toggle to see 'invoice view' vs 'engineering view'.
[02:28] Sara Malik: toggle meaning we can show internal vs external costs?
[02:32] Riley Chen: yeah, engineering view shows raw token counts and per-call latency; invoice view applies committed discounts, overage, and any enterprise add-ons.
[02:42] Jamie Park: and for internal chargeback, you can export a CSV per route. riley, can you show an example export?
[02:50] Riley Chen: export is here — downloads a CSV with columns: timestamp, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd, request_id. i'll click to generate... (brief pause) generated — sample link shared in chat.
[03:12] Priya Nair: about the request_id — is that PII? we need to ensure request bodies aren't stored.
[03:18] Riley Chen: good point. by default request_ids are UUIDs; payloads are not stored in the console unless you opt in for debug logging. we persist metadata (route, model, tokens) for analytics and audit. payload redaction is possible and we support retention policies per customer.
[03:36] Sara Malik: ok that helps. can we map cost to our internal cost centers? like attach tags?
[03:42] Riley Chen: yes, we support tagging at the API key and route level; tags flow through to exports and dashboards so you can group by product line.
[03:50] Tom Reyes: about caching, you mentioned prefix cache and KV cache, is it automatic?
[03:56] Riley Chen: we do automatic prefix caching for identical prompt prefixes and we also support application-managed KV caches. console shows cache hits and estimated token savings — see the blue shaded area on this chart. note that caching is conservative to avoid incorrect responses, so some dynamic prompts won't cache.
[04:18] Sara Malik: latency breakdown — we need p50, p95, p99 per route.
[04:22] Riley Chen: yep p50/p95/p99 are shown; you can drill into a time window and see per-model percentiles. we also show model warm/cold effects (kv cache warmup) and breakdown of server time vs network time.
[04:38] Alex Gomez: there's also a route-level SLA overlay — you can set an SLO and get alerted when p95 exceeds threshold.
[04:44] Tom Reyes: can we correlate latency regressions with model changes?
[04:47] Riley Chen: yes - model versioning ties into the dashboard. when you roll a new model version the console shows a before/after for selected metrics (latency, cost, quality signals). we also integrate with our regressions alerts in Optimize.
[05:00] Sara Malik: quality signals?
[05:02] Riley Chen: short version: you define eval sets and Redwood runs periodic evals comparing model outputs; we surface quality regression alerts tied to routes and prompts.
[05:12] Jamie Park: switching to cost breakdown — this is where teams usually get excited or a bit nervous.
[05:18] Riley Chen: cost breakdown card shows Token cost, compute surcharge for dedicated (if applicable), caching savings, and any external charges like third-party embeddings. we also show per-1k-token effective price after reserved capacity amortization.
[05:34] Tom Reyes: compute surcharge? what's that?
[05:36] Riley Chen: for Dedicated, there's a small surcharge that accounts for GPU time that isn't fully utilized by your traffic — basically amortized infra cost. for hosted customers it's a straightforward per-token price.
[05:48] Sara Malik: can we set alerts on cost spikes?
[05:51] Riley Chen: yes you can set cost thresholds per route or per tag and get alerts via Slack/email/webhook. you can also set automatic routing fallbacks if cost per token exceeds a threshold — e.g., route to smaller model once cost threshold hit.
[06:08] Priya Nair: regarding routing, does Redwood do smart routing across variants for latency vs cost?
[06:13] Riley Chen: yes — we have smart routing policies. you can set primary route to a high-quality model, with a secondary cheaper model as fallback; policies can be based on latency, cost, region, or custom signals. there's also an A/B rollout option for testing a new model version on a percentage of traffic.
[06:33] Tom Reyes: will fallback change token accounting and billing?
[06:37] Riley Chen: accounting is per request and per model — if fallback triggers the route will show both primary and fallback counts. the console tags them so you can attribute cost and quality to each decision.
[06:46] Sara Malik: security stuff: SSO, SAML, RBAC, and KMS. how do those map to console and logs?
[06:53] Riley Chen: SSO/SAML for SSO providers is supported; RBAC allows you to restrict views (billing-only, infra-only). KMS integration is available for Private and Dedicated customers — keys managed in your KMS/HSM; we support envelope encryption so Redwood never has plaintext keys. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM.
[07:12] Priya Nair: is on-prem available? we have some regulated workloads.
[07:16] Jamie Park: yes we have Private deployment for VPC/on-prem; the console runs in your control plane and connects to Redwood's control plane for management. for fully air-gapped you can get an on-prem package. we'll share the SOC2 and architecture docs.
[07:30] Liam O'Connor: procurement question — if we go dedicated reserved capacity, how are overages handled?
[07:37] Jamie Park: usually you commit to a capacity for the term; overages are billed at an agreed overage rate. we can include burst capacity for occasional peaks; we showed committed burst in the deck. i'll include the pricing examples in the docs.
[07:50] Sara Malik: real quick — can you show the route-level dashboard for a hypothetical /summary route with a lot of short responses?
[07:58] Riley Chen: sure — opening a mock route. here you see average tokens in is 18, tokens out 32, p95 is 340ms, estimated cost $0.0042 per request at our hosted price. cache hit is 12% which saved about $120 last month.
[08:20] Tom Reyes: the numbers seem optimistic vs our latency goals. what hardware is behind dedicated?
[08:25] Riley Chen: Dedicated runs on curated GPU types — for example A100 or H100 variants depending on the model. we publish performance profiles per model and we can run a benchmark with your payload.
[08:36] Tom Reyes: can you run a perf benchmark with our prompt set and 99p latency target of 500ms?
[08:41] Riley Chen: yes — that's a standard pilot. we'll need sample traffic and we can run it in our dedicated staging cluster. that will give you realistic p99 and throughput numbers.
[08:51] Sara Malik: regarding cost breakdown exports, can we integrate with our FinOps tooling?
[08:56] Riley Chen: exports are S3/GS compatible and you can set up a scheduled job to push to your cost pipeline. we also have a billing API for automated ingestion.
[09:06] Alex Gomez: one more Optimize feature — we can recommend quantization profiles and batching strategies tailored to your token distribution; Optimize suggests mode changes to save cost and shows simulated savings.
[09:20] Tom Reyes: how safe are those quantization recommendations for quality? we can't regress user-facing summaries.
[09:26] Riley Chen: Optimize runs A/B evals on a sample set; we only recommend quantization that passes quality thresholds you set. it's conservative and you can opt to run it in canary before full rollout.
[09:38] Sara Malik: can you tie quality regressions to the console alerts?
[09:41] Riley Chen: yep. if an eval shows a negative quality delta, it can trigger a regression alert and optionally roll back to the previous model.
[09:48] Jamie Park: we've covered a lot — i'm going to open the Q&A.
[09:53] Liam O'Connor: procurement — do you support net 60 payment terms for enterprise deals?
[09:57] Jamie Park: yes we can negotiate payment terms on enterprise contracts; we'll engage legal after pilot sizing.
[10:04] Priya Nair: data residency — can we keep logs in eu-only region?
[10:08] Riley Chen: for hosted we have region controls; you can pin data residency and logs to eu-only. for Private it's entirely in your control.
[10:15] Tom Reyes: small thing — does console show per-model memory and kv cache size so we can estimate cold start times?
[10:21] Riley Chen: we show model memory footprints and estimated kv cache size metrics per route; cold start impact is highlighted on the latency chart.
[10:30] Sara Malik: can we create custom dashboards per stakeholder? product managers want simple cost per feature view.
[10:35] Riley Chen: yes — custom dashboards and role-specific saved views are supported. PMs can see cost per feature via tags and route grouping.
[10:42] Jamie Park: i'll demo the route alerting quickly — set a policy to notify slack #infra-billing when daily cost exceeds $500.
[10:49] Riley Chen: creating policy... selecting channel... saved. policy executed and we can simulate a spike to verify.
[11:02] Tom Reyes: side question — how does billing work for embeddings? separate or same?
[11:07] Riley Chen: embeddings appear as distinct line items; console groups them under 'embedding calls' and shows per-unit embedding price. you can attribute embeddings to routes if your app calls embeddings under the same route.
[11:18] Sara Malik: we run both embeddings and chat models — can Redwood suggest batching and caching settings per route?
[11:24] Riley Chen: yes Optimize will suggest batching windows, KV-cache TTLs, and recommend quantization levels; it will estimate savings and the impact on latency.
[11:34] Jamie Park: ok let's talk pilot scope — generally it's a 4-week technical pilot: week 0 onboarding and instrumentation, week 1 perf runs, week 2 real traffic testing, week 3 cost & quality evaluation. does that timeline fit?
[11:49] Sara Malik: that seems reasonable — we have a launch target in Q3 so a mid-April pilot is ok.
[11:55] Tom Reyes: for instrumentation, which SDKs do you support?
[11:58] Riley Chen: SDKs for Python, Node, and Java — plus a lightweight HTTP client. we'll share examples for tagging and metrics.
[12:06] Priya Nair: about logs and audit exports: are they push or pull?
[12:10] Riley Chen: both — we can push to your S3, or you can pull via API. SIEM integrations via Kafka or SQS are also possible.
[12:20] Sara Malik: any additional compliance docs we should review? SOC2? ISO?
[12:24] Jamie Park: we'll share SOC2, ISO, and our architecture & KMS docs. adding that to next steps.
[12:30] Riley Chen: two quick notes on console UX — one is the invoice vs engineering toggle we demoed; second is the 'model snapshot' feature where you can pin a version to avoid accidental rollouts.
[12:44] Tom Reyes: that's helpful. will the pinning prevent auto-fallbacks?
[12:47] Riley Chen: pinning prevents automatic rollouts but fallback policies for cost/latency still apply unless you disable them for that route.
[12:55] Sara Malik: any gotchas on replays? if we want to replay traffic to benchmark, do you store the payloads?
[13:01] Riley Chen: we don't store payloads by default; for replay you can provide sanitized payloads or enable ephemeral debug storage for the pilot under strict retention.
[13:12] Jamie Park: wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners. Jamie send pricing + dedicated capacity examples; Riley share console screenshots + mock route exports; Tom share sample traffic; Sara to schedule pilot kickoff. we'll also send SOC2/KMS docs.
[13:31] Sara Malik: thanks, Jamie, Riley. quick commercial ques — do you have prepaid committed credits?
[13:36] Jamie Park: yes, we offer committed reserved capacity and prepaid credits, both shown in the pricing deck.
[13:42] Liam O'Connor: ok i'm good, thanks.
[13:45] Jamie Park: great, i'll follow up with meeting notes and links (jamie@redwood.example). any final q's?
[13:52] Tom Reyes: none from me.
[13:54] Priya Nair: none.
[13:56] Riley Chen: thanks everyone. bye.

End of transcript.
